title: Printable coordinate grid sheet (lesson 68)
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y8 lesson 68 (Printable coordinate grid sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 68: Reflections in y = x and y = -x; describing reflections. To understand how to reflect in the lines y = x and y = -x and describe a reflection fully by its mirror line

model.title: Reflect the triangle (1, 3), (2, 6), (4, 3) in the line y = x.
(1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 4) maps to (1, -4), (3, -4), (3, -6). Describe the transformation fully.

questions.q: Reflect (4, 7) in y = x and in y = -x.
questions.model: y = x: swap, (7, 4). y = -x: swap and change both signs, (-7, -4).

questions.q: (a) Reflect the triangle (1, 1), (4, 1), (1, 2) in y = x. (b) Reflect it in y = -x. (c) Describe fully: (2, 3), (5, 3), (5, 4) maps to (2, -1), (5, -1), (5, -2). (d) Describe fully: (0, 1), (2, 1), (2, 4) maps to (6, 1), (4, 1), (4, 4).
questions.model: (a) Swap each pair: (1, 1) stays (it is on the line), (4, 1) → (1, 4), (1, 2) → (2, 1). (c) Midpoint of y = 3 and y = -1 is y = 1; check the others: 4 and -2 also give 1.

questions.q: Which points do not move when reflected in y = x?
questions.a: Every point on the line y = x, such as (3, 3): they are invariant

questions.q: Reflect (2, 5) in the x-axis, then reflect the result in the y-axis. What single transformation does the same?
questions.a: (-2, -5): a rotation of 180° about the origin

questions.q: Big question: how do you find the mirror line from an object and its image?
questions.a: Find the midpoints of each point and its image; the mirror line passes through them all (the perpendicular bisector).
